Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A municipal records office files inspection paperwork through a standardized intake queue, assigns a docket number, indexes the document by property address and inspection date, and stores the final disposition in a fire-code registry.

2) What occurred: The actor submitted a dated request to the fire-code registry citing an outstanding violation docket. The actor opened a communication channel with an inspector account and recorded a payment offer referencing an undocumented settlement figure. The actor requested alteration of the inspection status field in the docket record from "failed" to "passed." The actor created a secondary correspondence document bearing the date of the original inspection but describing a completed remediation. The actor directed the inspector account to attach the secondary document to the primary docket. The actor instructed deletion of the original communication channel logs within a defined date range. The actor filed the amended docket under the same property address and docket number.

3) Materials/access observed: A docket record with a docket number, property address, and inspection date fields. A disposition field within the docket record. An inspector account with administrative access to the registry. A payment reference field in the correspondence. Two documents bearing the same inspection date. The communication channel log.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Two documents with identical inspection dates but differing content. A docket status field value inconsistent with the original inspection timestamp. A payment reference without a corresponding municipal receipt record. A communication channel with logs absent for a defined date range. A docket number with multiple disposition entries on the same date.
